chapter: Charlie Johnson, Willie Gant and the late 1920s
title: Charlie Johnson's band personnel
summary: He returned to Charlie Johnson for about a year with Jimmy Harris, Tommy Ladnier, Benny Carter, Benny Waters and others.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, Charlie Johnson -- for how long did that go on?
I worked with Charlie after Willie Gant band came out. I went back there to work with Charlie, oh, about a year.
And who was in that band then?
Oh, Leonard Hannon Davis, Jimmy Harris on trombone, Tommy Ladnier on trumpet.
Oh, Tommy Ladnier (unintelligible)?

Yes, uh-huh, Tommy Ladnier; Benny Carter was on alto. Let me see now. Who else was there? Benny Waters was there, but he had -- he left on account of he had an operation for his tonsils, and they came after me to play. And they had Billy Taylor. No, wasn't Billy Taylor -- Cy St. Clair was on bass, playing bass tuba.
Well, that's interesting, what you said about Tommy. (He Doesn't he have that (unintelligible)?
Yeah, and Charlie Johnson on the piano; Bobby Johnson was the banjo player.
From Boston.
Yeah, that's Howard Johnson's brother.
Right.
And I think we had -- that's the

brass section, because, yeah, Tommy Gardner was on trumpet. But sometimes them fellows didn't all -- like -- of course, Jimmy worried all the wasn't only a trumpet player. Jimmy was a terrific trombone player.
He was already then, in '26?

Yeah, he was there, because Jack Teagarden, him and Jack was good buddies, formed a good friendship. And Jack just come out of there, leave Ben Pollack's Pollard's band (unintelligible) down around town. All of them come uptown, Tommy Dorsey, Jack Teagarden, Frank -- Frankie Clarice Trombone and quite a few. Johnny had a very good band -- oh, Sidney DeParis came in after Tommy left, Sidney DeParis.
After who left?
After Tommy left, yeah.
Well, when Tommy was in, that was after he came back from Europe.
Right, that's right.
Well, he probably wasn't there long.
No, he wasn't there long.
(Simultaneous remarks)
Now, he was another guy that -- of course, after Fletcher he more or less disappeared.
Yes, he did. He -- happen (unintelligible)
